title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Improves continuous batcher scheduling fairness and reduces starvation by adding per-client fairness weights, max-wait timeouts, and improved queue backpressure handling. Default behavior is backward compatible. Config knobs exposed: scheduler.max_queue_time_ms, scheduler.fairness_weight, scheduler.min_batch_fill_ratio, scheduler.starvation_timeout_ms.
description: Motivation: Customers and internal perf runs showed intermittent starvation and elevated p95/p99 latency for small, latency-sensitive requests when the continuous batcher tried to maximize GPU utilization. This PR adjusts scheduler heuristics and adds safety timeouts to improve fairness and reduce tail latency without regressing throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced per-client fairness weights and a soft priority queue so long-running/high-throughput tenants do not monopolize batch slots; 2) Added a starvation_timeout_ms that forces a pending request to be scheduled after a maximum wait; 3) Implemented a max_queue_time_ms that triggers a backpressure path and optional direct-routing to a lower-latency model variant when queue time exceeds threshold; 4) Tuned min_batch_fill_ratio to prefer lower latency small batches for latency-sensitive routes while preserving batching efficiency for bulk workloads; 5) KV cache interaction: update scheduling to favor requests that will hit prefix KV cache to avoid needless recomputation and reduce cold-KV eviction thrash; 6) Added configuration flags and a feature gate continuous_batcher_v2 to enable gradual rollouts. Checklist: updated unit tests; added perf microbench harness; added integration test covering starvation scenarios; documented new config knobs in runbook. Compatibility: All defaults maintain prior behavior except when the feature gate is enabled. Rollout plan: Enable behind feature gate in canary pool for 48 hours, gather p95/p99 signals and throughput delta, then promote. Perf results from internal bench: 12-18% p99 reduction for small-req workflows, 8-12% p95 improvement across mixed workloads, throughput within 2% of baseline on steady-state large-batch tests. Related work: previous continuous-batcher scheduler tuning PRs ENG-3782, ENG-3810 and incident SUP-9123. This PR contains the implementation, tests and documentation updates.
